assessment.nobel_worthiness: Liquid-liquid phase separation as an organizing principle of the cell is a genuinely new concept of molecular organisation: membraneless condensates formed by multivalent interactions, described with polymer physics and phase-diagram thinking. It brings thermodynamics and soft-matter physical chemistry into the centre of cell biology, with very broad downstream impact on neurodegeneration, signalling and gene regulation.
assessment.attribution: Hyman and Brangwynne's 2009 P-granule work established the liquid-like behaviour and the idea; Rosen's multivalent-interaction (SH3/PRM) work supplied the quantitative physical-chemical basis. Pappu and Mittag are important on sequence grammar but I would keep the prize to three. The Hyman-Brangwynne priority is clearer than the third slot.
assessment.maturity: Rapidly confirmed and widely reproduced as a concept, with strong independent support in vitro. Still, the field is debating which cellular condensates are truly phase-separated and what is functionally essential, so timing is somewhat early but defensible.
uncertainties: How many in-cell condensates are genuine equilibrium phase separation versus other assemblies is debated.
Choice of third laureate among Rosen, Pappu and Mittag is unresolved.
My knowledge of the latest controversies is from memory, not verified.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles are lipid self-assembly applied to a hard physical-chemical problem: encapsulating nucleic acids, controlling pKa-dependent charge and membrane fusion for endosomal release. The clinical consequence, enabling siRNA drugs and mRNA vaccines, is enormous and the underlying design principles are clearly chemical.
assessment.attribution: Cullis with Hope and Madden developed the core LNP formulation and the ionizable-lipid and microfluidic-mixing concepts at UBC. Other credited people (MacLachlan, Anderson, Langer) made important contributions to siRNA and lipid libraries, so credit is spread. Three UBC-centred names give the cleanest configuration but would be contested.
assessment.maturity: Mature: approved Onpattro in 2018 and billions of vaccine doses, with independent confirmation. Recognition is timely, though the 2023 Medicine prize for mRNA modification partly overlaps in application.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2023 Medicine prize could be seen as redundant.
Which formulators and lipid chemists are decisive is genuinely disputed, including Anderson and Langer.
Relative weight of the ionizable lipid structure versus the delivery concept is unclear.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The energy-landscape and funnel view of protein folding explains how a random-looking chain reaches a unique structure, using statistical mechanics, frustration and thermodynamic ideas. It resolved Levinthal's paradox conceptually and shaped how folding, misfolding and aggregation (including amyloid) are understood. It is a core physical-chemistry concept.
assessment.attribution: Wolynes, Onuchic and Bryngelson developed the funnel and minimal-frustration theory; Dill's hydrophobic-collapse and lattice-model contributions are parallel and important. Fersht gave key experimental phi-value mapping. Selecting three from five leaves difficult choices that might look arbitrary.
assessment.maturity: The concept is foundational and widely accepted, long confirmed experimentally and by simulation. The 2024 prize on structure prediction did not recognise the physics of folding, so there is a plausible case now, though the theory is more conceptual than a single decisive discovery.
uncertainties: Whether to include Fersht (experimental) in place of Dill is unresolved.
Credit among theorists is entangled across several groups.
The 2024 prize could make the committee feel the folding area is already covered.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Palladium-catalysed C-N cross-coupling (Buchwald-Hartwig amination) is a transformative synthetic method that is routine in pharmaceutical and materials chemistry. The ligand design and mechanistic understanding turned a niche reaction into a general tool. Though synthesis is outside my own field, it is a clear, high-impact chemistry contribution.
assessment.attribution: Buchwald and Hartwig independently developed the general catalytic systems and made decisive ligand and mechanistic advances in the mid-1990s onward. Kosugi's earlier tin-amide coupling is an important precedent but is less general. Two laureates is a clean configuration, with some risk about precedent credit.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature after three decades of use, strongly confirmed and widely adopted. Timing is arguably overdue, though cross-coupling was already recognised in 2010, which could count against it.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2010 cross-coupling prize may reduce appetite.
Kosugi precedent credit may be raised.
I am less able to judge the synthetic-field ranking against other synthesis candidates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Targeted protein degradation reframes drug action as induced proximity chemistry, with PROTACs and molecular glues hijacking E3 ligases to remove proteins. It opens targets thought undruggable, and the mechanistic link to thalidomide and cereblon is a satisfying chemical-biological story. Clinical trials of degraders are advancing.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies conceived and demonstrated the PROTAC concept; Ciulli made key structure-guided VHL-ligand and ternary-complex contributions. Handa, Ito and Sakamoto are also credited and the glue-versus-PROTAC credit allocation is not tidy. Deciding between these subfields matters.
assessment.maturity: Impact is rising but clinical validation is still limited, as no degrader is yet a widely approved drug; the concept itself is well confirmed by many groups. Possibly slightly early.
uncertainties: No broadly approved PROTAC drug yet, so patient impact is still prospective.
Allocation between PROTACs and molecular glues (Handa, Ito, Gray) is disputed.
Choice of Ciulli versus Sakamoto or Gray is uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Proton-coupled electron transfer is a central concept linking physical chemistry, bioinorganic chemistry and energy conversion, explaining how electrons and protons move together in photosynthesis, respiration and catalysts. The combination of theory and molecular electrocatalysis gives it depth and conceptual clarity of the kind I value.
assessment.attribution: Mayer and Nocera developed the experimental PCET framework and model systems; Hammes-Schiffer provided the theoretical treatment of vibronic coupling. Meyer's earlier contributions complicate credit and he is credited alongside, so the choice excludes a senior figure.
assessment.maturity: Well established and used widely, with theory and experiment cross-confirmed. Recognition is plausible now, though the area is diffuse and less compact as a single discovery than others.
uncertainties: The discovery is a framework rather than a single event, which makes citation of a prize motivation difficult.
Exclusion of Thomas J. Meyer is a notable attribution risk.
Practical impact on technology is less direct than in other candidates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Car-Parrinello molecular dynamics made it possible to simulate atoms moving with forces computed from electronic structure on the fly, enabling studies of liquids, water, reactions and condensed phases from first principles. It is a landmark of computational physical chemistry with enduring influence on simulation of chemical systems.
assessment.attribution: Credit is clean: the 1985 paper by Car and Parrinello is the unambiguous origin, giving a natural two-person prize. Parrinello also appears in other candidates (machine-learned potentials, metadynamics), so the committee must consider how it weighs his total contribution.
assessment.maturity: Very mature, with four decades of use and many confirmations. Recognition is arguably overdue, though DFT and computational methods were recognised in 1998 and 2013, which might reduce the sense of gap.
uncertainties: Overlap with Parrinello's other candidacies could lead to a combined framing question.
Prior computational chemistry prizes may count against it.
I am uncertain of the exact weight the committee gives purely methodological advances.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Self-assembled monolayers of thiols on gold and the associated soft-lithography methods established molecular-level control over surfaces and interfaces. This is classic colloid and surface chemistry, showing how spontaneous organisation can be harnessed, and it underpins sensors, microfluidics and biointerface studies.
assessment.attribution: Nuzzo and Allara reported the thiol and disulfide monolayers on gold in 1983, and Whitesides developed SAMs systematically plus soft lithography. Sagiv's earlier silane monolayers complicate priority, and Xia is credited for soft lithography. Credit is plausible but contested.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature with extensive confirmation, though the main impact peaked years ago; the prize case may be seen as late, and some of the concept was folded into later nanoscience prizes.
uncertainties: Priority dispute with Sagiv's earlier monolayer work.
Whitesides' contributions are broad, so the specific prize motivation is hard to define.
Contemporary relevance may be judged lower than newer fields.
